key_insight: Adaptive optimization of discretized PDEs can recover highly accurate self-similar singularity profiles without domain truncation or prescribed far-field conditions.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers computational scientists a high-accuracy numerical tool for studying singular behavior that complements AI-based methods.
method: Represent fields with overlapping local Chebyshev patches and a mapped asymptotic patch.
Factor out leading power laws and optimize the limiting amplitudes at infinity.
Refine using Chebyshev-coefficient decay and solve with automatically differentiated Gauss–Newton iterations and Levenberg–Marquardt damping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports O(10^-14)-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^-14) to O(10^-10) for generalized De Gregorio equations, and O(10^-8) residuals locally for 2D Boussinesq equations.
watch_item: Small numerical residuals do not by themselves prove singularity formation, and the reported Boussinesq residual is local rather than global.
paper_title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
